guarantees.claim: wipe_secret is driven by reg2hw's wipe_secret.qe signal
wipe_v is driven by reg2hw's wipe_secret.q signal
digest_size_started_d is digest_size when hash_start_or_continue is true, else digest_size_started_q
key_length_supplied is a cast of cfg_reg.key_length.q to key_length_e type
err_valid is asserted when ~hmac_err.q and any of hash_start_sha_disabled, update_seckey_inprocess, hash_start_active, msg_push_not_allowed, invalid_config_atstart are true
guarantees.cond: when hmac_err.q is not set and any listed condition is true

assumptions.claim: reg2hw.wipe_secret.qe and .q must be correctly driven by external logic to enable proper secret wipe
assumptions.risk: secret data may not be wiped, leaving sensitive material

assumptions.claim: digest_size must be a legal and stable value when hash_start_or_continue is asserted
assumptions.risk: incorrect digest size leads to incorrect HMAC computation

assumptions.claim: cfg_reg.key_length.q must contain a legal value for the key_length_e enum
assumptions.risk: key_length_supplied may be X or invalid, causing key length mis-interpretation

assumptions.claim: error condition signals (hash_start_sha_disabled, etc.) must be correctly asserted and stable
assumptions.risk: err_valid may miss errors or falsely trigger, affecting error handling

uncertain_points.claim: err_valid gated by ~hmac_err.q may prevent detection of new errors while hmac_err is already set; intention unclear
uncertain_points.cond: when hmac_err.q is high and a new error occurs
uncertain_points.risk: system may miss important error conditions

uncertain_points.claim: wipe_secret derived from .qe and wipe_v from .q; need to confirm that qe correctly pulses and q holds intended wipe value
uncertain_points.risk: secret may not be wiped or may be wiped with incorrect value

uncertain_points.claim: no validation that cfg_reg.key_length.q is within key_length_e enum before cast; invalid value could propagate X
uncertain_points.risk: key length processing failure, leading to security weakness

uncertain_points.claim: in_process and initiated are declared but not driven or used in this chunk; check if they are assigned elsewhere
uncertain_points.risk: if not driven, they remain X, potentially causing downstream issues
